definitions.explanation: The daughter of a prince, duke, or other high-ranking nobleman. Used primarily in European historical and literary contexts when translated into Japanese.

examples.japanese: {公女|こうじょ}は{城|しろ}で{育|そだ}った。
examples.english: The princess grew up in a castle.

examples.japanese: {物語|ものがたり}の{主人公|しゅじんこう}はある{国|くに}の{公女|こうじょ}だった。
examples.english: The protagonist of the story was a princess of a certain country.

examples.japanese: {歴史小説|れきししょうせつ}では{公女|こうじょ}たちの{政略結婚|せいりゃくけっこん}がよく{描|えが}かれる。
examples.english: In historical novels, political marriages of princesses are often depicted.

notes:
Composed of {公|こう} (duke, public, noble) and {女|じょ} (woman, daughter). Primarily used as a translation equivalent for European titles like "princess" or "duke's daughter" in historical and literary contexts. Not used for Japanese imperial princesses, who are called {皇女|こうじょ} (same pronunciation, different first kanji).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {皇女|こうじょ} — imperial princess (daughter of an emperor; same reading, different kanji)
- {王女|おうじょ} — princess (daughter of a king)
- {姫|ひめ} — princess, young lady (broader, more common in daily speech and stories)
- {令嬢|れいじょう} — young lady of good family (not specifically noble)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {公女|こうじょ}の{身分|みぶん} — the status of a princess
- {公女|こうじょ}として{育|そだ}つ — to be raised as a princess
